# Streaming reference

Every class in `assets/scripts/streaming/`, from its doc comments. The overview is in [README.md](README.md).

- [ChunkStreamer](#chunkstreamer)
- [PawnStreamingSource](#pawnstreamingsource)

## ChunkStreamer

`res://assets/scripts/streaming/ChunkStreamer.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

Loads terrain chunks around every streaming source, and unloads the ones nothing needs any more, without stalling the game.

Add it to the scene and set its `terrain` (a [`WorldCoordinator`](../world/REFERENCE.md#worldcoordinator) does this, and turns off the terrain's `build_on_start`), then add a [`StreamingSource`](#streamingsource) to whatever should keep the world loaded; a pawn that does is a source itself. Building a chunk is split into steps (`TerrainGenerator.build_chunk_step()`) and each frame runs steps until `max_ms_per_frame` is used up, so a slower machine finishes chunks later but its frames stay short. The chunks directly under a source are built at once, right before each tick, outside the budget, so a pawn has ground on its first tick. A chunk loads within a source's load_distance and only unloads past load_distance + `unload_margin`. Each machine runs its own streamer; terrain isn't sent, since the same settings build the same ground. Design: streaming spec (docs/streaming/STREAMING_SPEC.md).

With the tick driver running, chunks land on ticks (state store spec 13.12): what's wanted is decided on ticks, each new chunk gets a landing tick (`landing_delay_ticks` on, no more than `max_landings_per_tick` a tick), building stops just before publishing (its points, collision and nav), and it's published before its landing tick runs, finishing it first if it isn't done. So the same start lands the same ground on the same ticks on any machine; each landing goes in the [`LandingLog`](../state_store/REFERENCE.md#landinglog).

### Settings and properties

- `terrain: TerrainGenerator`: The terrain to load chunks for. If it's empty and this node's parent is a terrain, it uses the parent.
- `max_ms_per_frame: float` = `2.0`: How long this may spend per frame, in milliseconds. At least one step always runs, so one step can go over.
- `unload_margin: float` = `64.0`: How far past a source's load_distance a chunk stays loaded, in metres, so that hovering around the edge doesn't rebuild it.
- `max_chunks_per_source: int` = `256`: The most chunks loaded per active source, a safety limit against running out of memory. Per source because a server needs chunks around every player. At the defaults a source wants about 37 chunks.
- `refresh_seconds: float` = `0.2`: How often to check where the sources are, in seconds. Shorter reacts faster and costs more.
- `hold_when_no_sources: bool` = `true`: With no active sources, keeps every chunk loaded. Off: they all unload.
- `landing_delay_ticks: int` = `30`: With the tick driver: ticks from when a chunk is wanted to when it lands, written for 60 ticks a second. Long enough for a machine to build it in the background; a machine that hasn't by then finishes it on that tick (a hitch).
- `max_landings_per_tick: int` = `2`: With the tick driver: the most chunks landing on one tick, so a burst of new chunks is spread over ticks.

### Signals

- `chunk_loaded(key: Vector2i)`: Sent when a chunk is completely built, including its collision.
- `chunk_unloaded(key: Vector2i)`: Sent when a chunk has been removed.

### Constants

- `MIN_GROUND_REACH = 2.0`: The nearest a chunk edge can be to a source before the next chunk is built straight away, in metres.
- `MAX_PREDICTED_MOVE = 8.0`: More than this between two checks, in metres, counts as a jump instead of movement. That's 480 m/s at 60 ticks a second.

### Functions

- `get_stats() -> Dictionary`: How things stand right now, as numbers for tests, stress runs and on-screen displays.
- `refresh_now() -> void`: Checks the sources now, instead of waiting for the next refresh. With the tick driver, before the next tick.
- `get_landing_tick(key: Vector2i) -> int`: The tick a chunk is due to land on, or -1 if none is scheduled.

## PawnStreamingSource

`res://assets/scripts/streaming/PawnStreamingSource.gd`, extends [`StreamingSource`](#streamingsource)

A pawn's streaming source: keeps the world loaded around its pawn while a player has it, or always with `keeps_world_loaded` on (a hero).

Every pawn gets one from the game's default parts (the PawnInitializer). It's in `StreamingSource.GROUP` only while it might count, so the chunk streamer, the nav feeder and replay look through the few pawns that matter, not the whole army. Its distances are the game's (`PawnDefaultsRes.world_load_distance` and `PawnDefaultsRes.world_nav_distance`), the same for every pawn: 320 and 128 m without them, and its own settings are hidden. The AI switch-off leaves a pawn on while this counts (`Pawn.is_keeping_world_loaded()`).

### Settings and properties

- `keeps_world_loaded: bool` = `false`: On: it keeps the world loaded around its pawn even without a player (a hero, say). Off (the default), only while a player has the pawn; a horde pawn freezes where nothing else keeps the ground loaded.
- `pawn: Pawn` = `null`: The pawn this is a part of, or null outside a pawn (then it never counts).

### Functions

- `counts_on_this_machine() -> bool`: Whether it keeps the world loaded on this machine now: a player has the pawn or `keeps_world_loaded` is on, and the pawn is simulated here (another player's pawn on a client doesn't count there).

## StreamingSource

`res://assets/scripts/streaming/StreamingSource.gd`, extends [`Node3D`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node3d.html)

Marks something as keeping the world loaded around it.

A [`ChunkStreamer`](#chunkstreamer) finds every source and loads chunks around the active ones. Add this as a child of whatever should keep the world loaded (an RTS camera, a spawner); it follows its parent, so it needs no code. Turn `active` off when it shouldn't count. A pawn's is a [`PawnStreamingSource`](#pawnstreamingsource), a default part, which counts while a player has the pawn.

**The source contract.** Anything in `GROUP` with these counts as a source; the chunk streamer, [`TerrainNavFeeder`](../world/REFERENCE.md#terrainnavfeeder), AIActivationManager and the replay read sources only through them:
- `global_position`, `load_distance`, `nav_distance` (metres).
- `counts_on_this_machine() -> bool` and `distance_moved_since_last_check() -> float`.

In multiplayer a source counts on the server or offline, and on a client only for that client's own pawn.

### Settings and properties

- `active: bool` = `true`: Whether this source keeps the world loaded right now. It can be changed at any time.
- `load_distance: float` = `320.0`: Chunks within this distance are loaded, in metres, measured to the nearest edge of the chunk.
- `nav_distance: float` = `128.0`: Nav is built within this distance, in metres. It's separate because nav has about 100 tiles per chunk at 128 m, so building it as far out as the ground would be slow. 0 means this source builds no nav. It can't exceed `load_distance`.

### Constants

- `GROUP = &"streaming_sources"`: The name of the Godot group every source joins, which is how a ChunkStreamer finds them.

### Functions

- `counts_on_this_machine() -> bool`: Whether this source should load chunks on this machine right now. ChunkStreamer asks this at every refresh. A pawn exists on every machine, so `active` alone would make each client load the world around every other player.
- `distance_moved_since_last_check() -> float`
